subject: history_social
notes: In 1979 psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky described a pattern they called loss aversion as part of a broader theory of how people decide under risk.
Loss aversion is the tendency to weigh a loss more heavily than a gain of the same size.
Experiments suggest that for many people a loss feels roughly twice as strong as an equal gain.
Many people refuse a coin toss in which they would win $150 if it lands heads but lose $100 if it lands tails, even though the expected gain is positive.
In one experiment, students who had been given a coffee mug demanded about twice as much to sell it as other students were willing to pay to buy one.
Loss aversion has become one of the most cited ideas in behavioral economics.
stem: The student wants to make a generalization about loss aversion and illustrate it with an example. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky described loss aversion in 1979 as part of a broader theory of how people make decisions under risk.
choices.B: People tend to feel a loss roughly twice as strongly as a gain of the same size, which is why many refuse a coin toss that would win them $150 or cost them $100.
choices.C: In one experiment, students who had been given a coffee mug demanded about twice as much to sell it as other students were willing to pay to buy one.
choices.D: Loss aversion is the tendency to weigh a loss more heavily than a gain of the same size, and it has become one of the most cited ideas in behavioral economics.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: a general statement about loss aversion and a specific case that shows it. Choice D gives the generalization and choice C gives an example, but each stops there. Only one choice states the general tendency and then shows it with the coin toss.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It tells who described loss aversion and when, with neither a generalization about the pattern itself nor an example.
explanation.B: Correct. "People tend to feel a loss roughly twice as strongly" is the generalization, and the coin toss is the example that illustrates it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It gives an example but no generalization, so the reader is not told what the example shows.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It states the generalization but offers no example, so it meets only half the goal.
